Each entry is the cross section in nb integrated over the corresponding four-dimensional bin; the bin volume is given in the last column of the table. The bin-averaged density (the cross section divided by the bin volume) is a derived quantity that is deliberately not tabulated, and model predictions must be integrated over the same bin volume before comparison with the tabulated values. The values are Born-level cross sections: they are corrected for detector effects and for radiative (QED and electroweak) effects; the correction convention is photon exchange only, i.e. the cross sections are defined without $Z$-boson exchange. Each cross section is quoted with its statistical uncertainty and its total systematic uncertainty. One correction factor, the applied photon-exchange-only radiative correction $C_{\gamma\mathrm{Born}}$, is tabulated with its uncertainty (sixth column). Dividing a tabulated cross section by the ratio $C_{\gamma\mathrm{Born}}/C_{\mathrm{rad}}$ of the same bin, with $C_{\mathrm{rad}}$ the corresponding factor of the convention with $Z$-boson exchange included, converts it to that convention. }
